# Tail ratio (95th / 5th percentile) (`tail_ratio`)

*Category: Tail behavior · Nature: estimated · Unit: ratio · Formula id: `tail_ratio@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Size of the right tail relative to the left tail.

## 2. Formula

```text
|Q_0.95(r)| / |Q_0.05(r)|
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

Above 1: the best periods were larger than the worst periods were bad.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Quantile-based asymmetry measure, robust to single extremes but noisy in short samples.

## 7. Assumptions

- Linear-interpolated empirical quantiles.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Few observations fall in the 5% tail: with monthly data a 95% estimate rests on roughly n/20 points.
- The history does not contain a stress period.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations; low confidence below n = 100. (policy `tail`: Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence when fewer than 5 observations are expected in the 5% tail (n < 100), moderate when fewer than 10 (n < 200).)

- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Absolute values of the 95th and 5th percentiles (decision 0010).
